title: Gluing integral constructibility of $f^!K$
statement:
1. Let $M\in D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal O_E)$ and let $(U_\alpha)$ be a finite
   open cover of $X$ with $M|_{U_\alpha}\in\Dbc(U_\alpha,\mathcal O_E)$ for all
   $\alpha$. Then $M\in\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$.
2. For $f:X\to Y$ separated of finite type and $K\in\Dbc(Y,\mathcal O_E)$,
   $f^!K\in\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$, and the adjunction $Rf_!\dashv f^!$ of
   [det-prop-int-brown-adjoint] restricts to an adjunction between
   $\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$ and $\Dbc(Y,\mathcal O_E)$.

proof.text: Exact open restriction. For an open $j:U\hookrightarrow X$, [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization] identifies $U_{\mathrm{proét}}$ with the slice $X_{\mathrm{proét}}/U$. The completed pulled-back coefficient ring restricts to the corresponding ring on $U$: sectionwise restriction commutes with the inverse limit in [det-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x-integral-limit]. Restriction of modules over this ring is exact by [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact]. Therefore applying it termwise to a representative computes derived restriction and gives $\mathcal H^q(j^*M)=j^*\mathcal H^q(M)$.

Global cohomological bounds. By [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible], each $M|_{U_\alpha}$ has cohomology in an interval $[r_\alpha,s_\alpha]$. For a nonempty finite cover take $r=\min_\alpha r_\alpha$ and $s=\max_\alpha s_\alpha$. Step 1 gives $\mathcal H^q(M)|_{U_\alpha}=0$ when $q\notin[r,s]$. For every site object $W\to X$, the maps $W\times_XU_\alpha\to W$ form a covering [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]; every section of $\mathcal H^q(M)$ restricts to zero there, and hence is zero by sheaf uniqueness. Thus $\mathcal H^q(M)=0$ outside $[r,s]$. If the cover is empty, $X$ is empty; the empty covering forces every module sheaf to be zero, so the conclusion holds directly.

Global constructibility. Fix $q$. On each $U_\alpha$, take the finite locally closed constructible stratification for $\mathcal H^q(M)|_{U_\alpha}$ of [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. Regard its strata as locally closed subsets of $X$ and add the closed complement $X\setminus U_\alpha$. Take all nonempty intersections of one piece from each resulting finite partition, realized as fibre products over $X$ of their chosen locally closed immersions. A finite intersection of subsets written as open intersect closed is again open intersect closed, so these fibre products give locally closed subschemes and form a finite disjoint partition; the standing schemes are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], applied to their structure morphisms over the field (whose only ideals are zero and the unit ideal), and their locally closed subsets are constructible by [def-weil-constructible-subset]. Each intersection lies in some $U_\alpha$ because these opens cover $X$, and hence in one of its local strata. The fibre-product projections map each refined stratum to its chosen local stratum. Base change of its trivializing pro-etale cover covers the refined stratum. Write the local model as the cokernel of a finite matrix $\mathcal O_{E,T}^{m}\to\mathcal O_{E,T}^{n}$ with entries in $\mathcal O_E$. Pullback is right exact and identifies the coefficient ring with $\mathcal O_{E,T'}$, as in [sk-def-sfb-constructible]; hence the pulled-back cokernel is presented by the identical scalar matrix over $\mathcal O_{E,T'}$ and has the required finite constant local model. Consequently $\mathcal H^q(M)$ is constructible by the cited definition. No assertion about finite reduction or comparison between two integral categories is used.

Conclusion of (1). Steps 2 and 3 show that $M$ is bounded and that every cohomology sheaf $\mathcal H^q(M)$ is constructible in the sense of [sk-def-sfb-constructible] (a finite stratification by constructible locally closed subschemes on whose strata it has a finite constant local model). The category $\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$ of the statement is, by [sk-def-sfb-constructible], the full subcategory of $D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal O_E)$ on the bounded complexes whose cohomology sheaves are constructible in exactly this sense, so $M\in\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$. Boundedness is the bounded-object condition recorded in [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible], which imposes no derived completeness. This is the category used by the Brown construction; no additional derived-completion condition or equivalence with a separately defined category is required.

Choose the affine charts for (2). Apply [det-thm-restriction-local] with its allowed coefficient $\Lambda=E$: its statement supplies finitely many affine source opens $u:U\hookrightarrow X$, affine target opens $v:V\hookrightarrow Y$, and closed immersions $i:U\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^d_V$ with projection $p:\mathbf A^d_V\to V$, such that the $U$ cover $X$ and $fu=vpi$. This use takes no rational-coefficient assertion about $f^!$. In the standing finite-type scheme setting [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting], the schemes are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], so these opens are quasi-compact and all these morphisms remain separated of finite type, so the integral Brown functors and the integral affine-space and closed-immersion statements apply to them.

source.place: (2), first sentence: finite affine covers and closed presentations

proof.text:
Integral open adjoints and composition. All schemes in the charts are separated of finite type over a field, hence qcqs. For integral coefficients the equality $\Dctf=\Dbc$, including equality of their localizing closures, is [det-def-localizing-closure-ctf-equals-bc]. Apply [det-sf-mate-open-restriction, clause 1] with $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$: for each chart open $w$, $w^!\cong w^*$ on the integral localizing categories. The last sentence of [det-prop-int-brown-adjoint] identifies this integral Brown right adjoint with the general one used by the open-restriction theorem on these equal categories. For composable $a:S\to T$ and $b:T\to R$, [det-prop-int-brown-construction] supplies $R(ba)_!\cong Rb_!Ra_!$, and [det-prop-int-brown-adjoint] supplies the three right adjoints. For any $A$ and $B$ in the corresponding localizing categories, composing their natural adjunction bijections gives
$$\operatorname{Hom}(R(ba)_!A,B)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(Ra_!A,b^!B)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(A,a^!b^!B).$$
Thus $a^!b^!$ is right adjoint to $R(ba)_!$, and the counit-compatible uniqueness in [det-prop-int-brown-adjoint] identifies $(ba)^!\cong a^!b^!$ after transporting the adjunction along the composition isomorphism for the left functors. For the equality $fu=vpi$ of Step 5 these identifications give
$$u^*f^!\cong u^!f^!\cong(fu)^!=(vpi)^!\cong i^!p^!v^!\cong i^!p^!v^*.$$
Every functor here has the integral coefficient $\mathcal O_E$.

source.place: (2), compatibility with composition and uniqueness of right adjoints

proof.text:
Apply the two previously separated geometric cases. For $K\in\Dbc(Y,\mathcal O_E)$, the inverse image $v^*K$ belongs to $\Dbc(V,\mathcal O_E)$ by [sk-lem-int-tensor]. Clauses 2 and 3 of [det-thm-int-restriction-line] give
$$p^!v^*K\cong p^*v^*K(d)[2d]\in\Dbc(\mathbf A^d_V,\mathcal O_E).$$
Apply [det-thm-int-restriction-closed] to this integral constructible input and the closed immersion $i$ to obtain $i^!p^!v^*K\in\Dbc(U,\mathcal O_E)$. The functor isomorphism of Step 6 therefore gives $u^*f^!K\in\Dbc(U,\mathcal O_E)$ on each member of the finite cover. Apply part (1), proved in Steps 1–4, to the underlying ambient derived object $f^!K$; hence $f^!K\in\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$.

Restrict the adjunction. The integral compact-support construction [det-prop-int-brown-construction] sends $A\in\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$ to $Rf_!A\in\Dbc(Y,\mathcal O_E)$, while Step 7 proves the corresponding property of $f^!$. Both integral categories $\Dbc(-,\mathcal O_E)$ are full subcategories of $D((-)_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal O_E)$ by [sk-def-sfb-constructible] (compare [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible]), and their localizing closures are full by [sk-def-localizing-closure]. Therefore the natural adjunction bijection of [det-prop-int-brown-adjoint] on the localizing categories, evaluated at $A$ and $K$, is a bijection between exactly the two Hom sets in the statement. Naturality is the same equality of composites for the same morphisms in these full subcategories. This supplies the restricted adjunction, with its inherited unit and counit.
